text:
maria: Quick question — customer wants Private deployment in GCP (us-central1 + asia-southeast1). They want us to pass through all cloud costs and also bill a Redwood license. How should we split pass-through infra vs license? and how do reserved GPU commitments factor in?

ajay: My instinct: show cloud charges as pass-through line items, then a separate platform/license line. But reserved commitments are messy — if we take a CUD/commit we probably need an amortization approach.

samir: Ops notes: if it's customer VPC/on-prem where they pay the cloud bill directly, it's easy. But for Private (Redwood-managed infra in customer network) we often sign the cloud contract, so we absorb the invoice then re-bill. That means we need a clear allocation method for committed discounts.

lina: Sales: we need a simple SOW clause. Something like: "Customer pays incurred cloud charges (billed monthly) + Redwood license fee." Also call out region differences (APAC egress/GPU premiums). :memo:

maria: Accounting/legal question — do we gross-bill (charge customer full amount) or net (show vendor cost as pass-through with zero margin)? Finance preference?

ajay: Finance preference is transparent pass-through lines + a small admin fee. Grossing up is possible but requires clear customer consent. We should avoid netting into one number for enterprise reviews.

samir: From ops: recommendation for amortization: take committed discount amount and allocate monthly over commitment period pro-rata to customers who used that reserved capacity. Example calc in BigQuery below.

samir: ```sql
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC(invoice_date, MONTH) AS month,
  sku.description AS sku,
  SUM(cost) AS total_cost
FROM `billing_export.gcp_invoices`
WHERE project_id LIKE '%private-%'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC;
```

maria: Good — two follow ups: 1) how to handle early customer termination (they leave but we still have a commit), 2) are there license vendor implications (per-host SKUs, HSM keys, etc.)?

lina: For termination we should add an early termination and pro-rata pass-back clause. Sales want a standard % to retain (e.g., 30 days of run-rate) to avoid weird tails.

kevin: legal: We need to make sure contract language covers "pass-through of third-party charges" + explicit list: compute, storage, egress, KMS/HSM, and support. Also call out currency and tax responsibility. I'll draft a clause. @maria will sync for redlines.

billing-bot: FYI — region price differences: APAC GPU SKUs ~15-25% higher; GST/VAT handling required for Singapore/Australia.

ops-bot: Provisioning note: when we create dedicated GPU pools for Private, tag with customer_id + commitment_bucket so billing export can join by labels.

maria: Action items:
- ajay: draft invoice template showing (a) cloud pass-through lines (b) license/platform line (c) admin fee
- samir: propose amortization method and example calc for a $200k 12-month GPU commit
- kevin: draft pass-through clause + early termination language
- lina: update SOW template with region surcharge note

ajay: I'll take the invoice template, aim for EOD Wed.

samir: I'll produce a sample amortization table and a BigQuery view to generate allocations.

maria: Cool. One last ask — do we want to put a default policy for how we price in multi-region commitments? e.g., apply commit discount to region of purchase first, then global pool? Thoughts?

lina: Default: tie commit to region where we purchased discount; if customer spans regions, explicitly call out cross-region surcharge. Keeps pricing defensible.

maria: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the working doc. Will escalate to legal and finance sync after first drafts. :+1:
